subproblems.title: Mass formula and support of an integer multiplicity current (Simon 6.3.2(3), 6.2.12)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep: M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ : ℝ^P → ℕ measurable with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and, Hⁿ-a.e. on M, equal to ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of the approximate tangent space) with T = τ(M, θ, ξ), i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Let μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure). Then (i) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) in [0, ∞] for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, where M_W(T) is the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (ii) spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Role in the parent proof: steps C1b–C1d (M_W(T) = μ_T(W) for open W; spt T = U ∩ spt μ_T), and the sibling stationary_of_minimizing uses (i). Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–765: M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ for open W) and Ch. 6, 2.11–2.12 (chapter-06.txt lines 295–307: spt T = spt μ_T). The book states both without proof; a complete proof follows. Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, μ_R = R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M. For an n-covector α, |α| = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm; I runs over strictly increasing multi-indices, e_I = (e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})), and dx^I denotes the coordinate covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ}. ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ means ξ(x)(α).
1. Pointwise algebra. Let x ∈ M be a point where R.orients holds: there are an orthonormal family τ₁, …, τₙ and s ∈ {1, −1} with ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) for every α. Expanding τ_j = Σ_i τ_j^i e_i, multilinearity and alternation give α(τ₁, …, τₙ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where det(τ^I) is the n×n minor of the matrix (τ_j^i) on the rows I; by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α. The covector ξ^♭(x) := Σ_I ⟨dx^I, ξ(x)⟩ dx^I has coefficients s·det(τ^I), hence |ξ^♭(x)| = 1 and ⟨ξ^♭(x), ξ(x)⟩ = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1. (For n = 0 the only I is empty: |α| = |α()|, ξ(x) = ±evaluation, ξ^♭(x) = ±1.) Since R.orients holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M and μ_R ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, these facts hold μ_R-a.e. The field x ↦ ξ^♭(x) is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable, being a continuous linear function of the a.e. strongly measurable ξ (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
2. Integral formula. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function x ↦ θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable: it is a.e. strongly measurable, vanishes off the compact set spt ω ⊆ U, is bounded by θ·sup|ω| a.e. (step 1), and ∫_{M∩spt ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). Hence T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R (integral with respect to the density θ).
3. Upper bound. Let W be open and ω admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), spt ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x). By step 1, ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for μ_R-a.e. x, and ω = 0 off W, so T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W) by step 2. Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
4. Lower bound. Let W be open and t a real number with t < μ_R(W); we construct an admissible ω with T(ω) > t, which proves M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞). Put G := W ∩ U (open). Since M ⊆ U, μ_R(G) = μ_R(W). μ_R is a Borel measure, finite on compact subsets of U; restricted to the open σ-compact set G it is a Radon measure (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15), hence inner regular by compact sets and outer regular on sets of finite measure. Fix η > 0 and a compact K ⊆ G with μ_R(K) > t + 4η. (a) Lusin (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17): there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < η such that ξ^♭ restricted to K' is continuous, and |ξ^♭| = 1, ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩ = 1 μ_R-a.e. on K'. (b) There is an open V with K' ⊆ V, V̄ compact, V̄ ⊆ G, and μ_R(V ∖ K') < η. (c) Extend the coefficients of ξ^♭ on K' continuously to ℝ^P (Tietze), compose with the radial retraction of Λⁿ(ℝ^P) onto its closed unit ball for |·|, and multiply by a continuous χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K', spt χ ⊆ V. The resulting continuous g has compact support in V, |g| ≤ 1 everywhere and g = ξ^♭ on K'. (d) Let g_ε := φ_ε ∗ g (coefficientwise convolution with a standard mollifier). For 0 < ε < dist(spt g, ℝ^P ∖ V), g_ε is C^∞ with compact support in V ⊆ W ∩ U, |g_ε(x)| ≤ ∫ φ_ε(x − y)|g(y)| dy ≤ 1 by convexity of the norm, and g_ε → g uniformly as ε → 0; so g_ε is admissible for M_W(T). (e) By steps 2 and 1, T(g_ε) = ∫⟨g_ε, ξ⟩ dμ_R ≥ ∫_{K'}⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R − ∫_{V∖K'}|⟨g, ξ⟩| dμ_R − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) ≥ μ_R(K') − η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) ≥ μ_R(K) − 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) > t + 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄). As μ_R(V̄) < ∞, T(g_ε) > t for small ε. Together with step 3 this proves (i): M_W(T) = μ_R(W).
5. Support. By definition (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support; Simon 2.11) spt T = U ∖ Z, where Z is the union of all open W with W̄ compact, W̄ ⊆ U and T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W. Recall x ∈ spt μ_R iff μ_R(B) > 0 for every neighbourhood B of x. (a) If x ∈ U ∩ spt μ_R and x ∈ Z, choose W in the union with x ∈ W; every admissible form for M_W(T) has T(ω) = 0, so M_W(T) = 0, hence μ_R(W) = 0 by (i), contradicting x ∈ spt μ_R. So U ∩ spt μ_R ⊆ spt T. (b) spt T ⊆ U by definition. If x ∈ U ∖ spt μ_R, choose r > 0 with μ_R(B_r(x)) = 0 and B̄_r(x) ⊆ U (U open). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_r(x), T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R = 0 by step 2; so B_r(x) is one of the sets forming Z, x ∈ Z and x ∉ spt T. Hence spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R, which is (ii).
proof_key_steps: For a unit simple n-vector ξ, |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Binet), with equality for the dual covector ξ^♭.
T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R, so admissible forms give T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W).
Lusin, Tietze extension, retraction and mollification of ξ^♭ give admissible forms with T(ω) arbitrarily close to μ_R(W).
The mass formula identifies the zero region of T with the complement of spt μ_R in U.

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity representation carries no H^n-mass off the support of the current
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (a GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) representing T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U). Then H^n(M ∖ spt T) = 0, where spt T = U ∖ ⋃{W : W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, T vanishes on W} (Simon 6.2.11).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ T.support) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: this is the fact "μ_T(U ∖ spt T) = 0" of step C1c of the parent proof, which C1e uses to get H^n(M_R ∖ N) = 0 from spt T ⊆ N (Simon 6.2.11 with 6.3.1; μ_T = θH^n⌞M by 6.3.2(3)).
1. Notation. M := R.carrier ⊆ U, θ := R.mult (θ ≥ 1 on M), ξ := R.orient, μ := μHE[n].restrict M. By definition T.support = U ∖ Z with Z := T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲, where 𝒲 is the family of open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W (T ω = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W). Since M ⊆ U, M ∖ T.support = M ∩ Z.
2. Countable reduction. ℝ^P is second countable, so ⋃𝒲 = ⋃_k W_k for a countable subfamily (W_k) ⊆ 𝒲 (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable). By countable subadditivity it suffices to show H^n(M ∩ W) = 0 for one fixed W ∈ 𝒲.
3. A finite measure. C := closure W is compact and C ⊆ U, so ∫_{M ∩ C} θ dH^n < ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult; since θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n(M ∩ C) < ∞. Put ν := μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C), a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P.
4. Orientation facts. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a plane Q and an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) spanning Q with ξ(x)(β) = s·β(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors β, s ∈ {1, −1}. At such x: (a) |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ (operator norm of the continuous alternating map, since |τ_i| = 1); (b) ξ(x) ≠ 0: the n-covector β_τ(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b} (for n = 0 the constant 1) is continuous, multilinear and alternating, and β_τ(τ) = det I = 1, so ξ(x)(β_τ) = s ≠ 0.
5. Testing T. Fix an n-covector α and set f_α(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(α). It is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable, ξ a.e. strongly measurable for μ ≥ ν) and |f_α| ≤ ‖α‖θ ν-a.e., so f_α ∈ L¹(ν). For every g ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P, ℝ) with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W, the form ω(x) := g(x)·α is smooth with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport in W. As T vanishes on W and R represents T: 0 = T ω = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(g(x)α) dH^n = ∫ g f_α dν (the integrand vanishes off W ⊆ C).
6. Fundamental lemma. Mathlib's IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero (open set W, measure ν, f_α locally integrable on W) gives: for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ θ(x)ξ(x)(α) = 0. Since θ ≥ 1 on M and ν is carried by M, ξ(x)(α) = 0 for ν-a.e. x ∈ W.
7. Conclusion. Let α_1, …, α_m be a basis of the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors on ℝ^P. Intersecting the finitely many full-measure sets of step 6, for ν-a.e. x ∈ W the linear functional ξ(x) vanishes on a basis, hence ξ(x) = 0. By step 4(b), ξ(x) ≠ 0 for μ-a.e. x, hence for ν-a.e. x. Therefore ν(W) = H^n(M ∩ C ∩ W) = H^n(M ∩ W) = 0, and by step 2, H^n(M ∖ T.support) = 0.
proof_key_steps: M ∖ spt T = M ∩ zeroRegion(T), a countable union of open W ⊂⊂ U on which T vanishes.
Testing T with g·α (g ∈ C_c^∞(W), α a constant covector) gives ∫ g θ ξ(α) dH^n⌞M = 0.
The fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations gives ξ = 0 a.e. on M ∩ W, while unit orientations are nonzero; hence H^n(M ∩ W) = 0.

subproblems.title: Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors versus Gram determinants (Cauchy–Binet)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n: (1) for every n-covector α on ℝ^P and v_1, …, v_n ∈ ℝ^P, |α(v_1, …, v_n)| ≤ |α|_E·(det(v_i·v_j)_{i,j})^{1/2}, where |α|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{i_1<⋯<i_n} α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of Simon 6.1.15; (2) for every orthonormal family τ_1, …, τ_n in ℝ^P there is an n-covector α with |α|_E ≤ 1 and α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (v : Fin n → Euclid P), |α v| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α * Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)))) ∧ ∀ τ : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ τ → ∃ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ 1 ∧ α τ = 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 6.1 (Λ^n with the inner product making e^{i_1}∧⋯∧e^{i_n} orthonormal, 6.1.15) and 6.3.4–3.5 (|v_1∧⋯∧v_n| = J); these are the algebraic facts behind "M_W(τ(M,θ,ξ)) = ∫_{M∩W}θ dH^n" (6.3.2(3)) and the Jacobian bound of the sibling first_variation_mass_bound (step C2d of the parent proof).
1. Notation. 𝓘 := the strictly increasing maps I : Fin n → Fin P; e_k := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ k; for I ∈ 𝓘, α_I := α(e_{I 1}, …, e_{I n}); by definition |α|_E = (Σ_{I∈𝓘} α_I²)^{1/2} (the sum over all I with the StrictMono filter). For v = (v_1, …, v_n) let V be the P×n matrix V_{k,j} := ⟨e_k, v_j⟩ = v_j(k), and for I ∈ 𝓘 let V_I be the n×n matrix (V_I)_{a,j} := v_j(I a).
2. Expansion. α(v) = Σ_{I∈𝓘} α_I·det V_I. Proof: write v_j = Σ_k v_j(k)e_k and expand by multilinearity: α(v) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_j v_j(f j))·α(e_{f 1}, …, e_{f n}). Terms with f not injective vanish (α alternating, repeated argument). Each injective f is uniquely f = I∘σ with I ∈ 𝓘 (the increasing enumeration of its range) and σ a permutation, and α(e_{I∘σ}) = sgn(σ)α_I. So α(v) = Σ_I α_I Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j v_j(I(σ j)) = Σ_I α_I det V_I by the Leibniz formula.
3. Cauchy–Binet. Σ_{I∈𝓘} (det V_I)² = det(VᵀV) = det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}. Proof: det(VᵀV) = Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i (Σ_k V_{k,i}V_{k,σ i}) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_i V_{f i, i})·Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i V_{f i, σ i} = Σ_f (Π_i V_{f i, i})·det(V_f), where V_f is the n×n matrix (V_{f a, j})_{a,j}. det V_f = 0 unless f is injective, and for f = I∘σ, det V_f = sgn(σ) det V_I (row permutation). Hence det(VᵀV) = Σ_I det V_I·Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i V_{I(σ i), i} = Σ_I (det V_I)² (Leibniz formula again).
4. Part (1). By step 2 and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in ℝ^𝓘, |α(v)| ≤ (Σ_I α_I²)^{1/2}(Σ_I (det V_I)²)^{1/2} = |α|_E·(det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩))^{1/2} by step 3 (the Gram determinant is ≥ 0, being a sum of squares).
5. Part (2). For n = 0 take α the constant 0-covector with value 1: |α|_E = 1 (𝓘 consists of the empty map) and α() = 1. For n ≥ 1 let α(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b}; it is multilinear, alternating and continuous, hence an n-covector, and α(τ) = det(⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = det I = 1. Moreover α_I = det(⟨τ_a, e_{I b}⟩)_{a,b} = det(T_I) with T the P×n matrix of τ (transposes have equal determinants), so by step 3 applied to v = τ: |α|_E² = Σ_I det(T_I)² = det(⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = 1. Hence |α|_E = 1 ≤ 1.
6. Degenerate cases are covered: if n > P then 𝓘 = ∅, |α|_E = 0, every n-covector vanishes (n vectors in ℝ^P are dependent) and there is no orthonormal n-family.
proof_key_steps: Expansion α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I) det V_I by multilinearity and alternation.
Cauchy–Binet: Σ_I (det V_I)² = det(v_i·v_j).
Cauchy–Schwarz gives (1); the covector u ↦ det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩) gives (2).

subproblems.title: The approximate tangent plane field of an integer multiplicity triple is measurable
subproblems.statement: For every integer multiplicity triple R = (M, θ, ξ) in a set U ⊆ ℝ^P (IMRep U n), the map x ↦ p_{T_xM}, the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x (the approximate tangent plane T_xM where it exists, {0} otherwise), is H^n⌞M-almost everywhere strongly measurable.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection) (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3 §1 (T_xM is unique, 1.5(1)) and the definition 6.3.1 of an integer multiplicity current, in which ξ orients T_xM in an H^n-measurable way; this measurability is implicit in Simon's formulas ∫ div_M X dμ_V (Ch. 4, 2.2–2.7), used by the siblings diffeo_pushforward and first_variation_mass_bound (steps C2c–C2d of the parent proof).
1. a.e. identification. Let μ := μHE[n].restrict M. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there is Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q_x. At such x the existential in the definition of approxTangentPlane holds, so approxTangentPlane n M x is some Q' with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q'; by uniqueness of approximate tangent planes (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) Q' = Q_x.
2. Case n = 0. Every Q with finrank 0 equals ⊥, and approxTangentPlane 0 M x is ⊥ in both branches of its definition, so the map is the constant 0, which is strongly measurable. Assume n ≥ 1.
3. A unit simple n-vector determines its plane. Let ζ ∈ (Λ^n)^* with ζ(β) = s·β(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors β, τ orthonormal, s = ±1. Claim: span τ = {v : ζ(ι_vβ) = 0 for every (n+1)-covector β}, where ι_vβ(u_1, …, u_n) := β(v, u_1, …, u_n). If v ∈ span τ then β(v, τ_1, …, τ_n) = 0 because the arguments are linearly dependent. If v ∉ span τ, let w := v − Σ_i⟨v, τ_i⟩τ_i ≠ 0 and β(u_0, …, u_n) := det(⟨c_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b=0..n} with c := (w, τ_1, …, τ_n), a continuous alternating (n+1)-form; the matrix (⟨c_a, (v, τ_1, …, τ_n)_b⟩) has first row (|w|², 0, …, 0) and lower-right block I_n, so β(v, τ) = |w|² and ζ(ι_vβ) = s|w|² ≠ 0. Consequently, if ζ orients both Q and Q' (IsUnitOrientationOf) then Q = Q'.
4. Continuity of the orientation-to-projection map. Let Ω := {(τ, s) : τ ∈ (ℝ^P)^n orthonormal, s ∈ {1, −1}}, a compact set, and Φ(τ, s) := (β ↦ s·β(τ)), a continuous map Ω → (Λ^n)^* (multilinear evaluation with |τ_i| = 1). Its image 𝒮 is compact, hence closed, and equals the set of ζ for which ∃ Q, IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q. The map G̃(τ, s) := Σ_i ⟨τ_i, ·⟩τ_i = starProjection(span τ) is continuous on Ω and, by step 3, constant on the fibres of Φ; hence G̃ = G∘Φ for a unique G : 𝒮 → End(ℝ^P). Since Φ : Ω → 𝒮 is a continuous surjection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff space, it is a quotient map, so G is continuous on 𝒮. Extend G by 0 outside 𝒮; the extension is Borel measurable (𝒮 closed, G continuous on it).
5. Conclusion. For μ-a.e. x (step 1), ξ(x) = Φ(τ, s) for an orthonormal basis τ of Q_x = approxTangentPlane n M x, hence starProjection(approxTangentPlane n M x) = G(ξ(x)). Since ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and G is Borel, G∘ξ is μ-a.e. measurable; End(ℝ^P) is finite-dimensional (second countable and metrizable), so G∘ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and so is the μ-a.e. equal map x ↦ (approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection.
proof_key_steps: Almost everywhere the approximate tangent plane is the plane oriented by ξ(x) (uniqueness of T_xM).
A unit simple n-vector determines its plane (kernel of v ↦ ζ(ι_v ·)).
The map unit simple n-vector ↦ projection is continuous on the compact set of such vectors (quotient-map argument); compose with the a.e.-measurable ξ.

subproblems.title: The tangent space of an embedded submanifold is the range of the derivative of any local representation
subproblems.statement: Let ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be a local representation of N ⊆ ℝ^P in the sense of Simon Ch. 2 §4 (4.1): V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P open, ψ of class C^r on V with r ≥ 1, ψ injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective for every z ∈ V. Then for every v ∈ V the tangent space T_{ψ(v)}N = {γ'(0) : γ ∈ C¹((−1,1); ℝ^P), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ N, γ(0) = ψ(v)} (tangentSpace N (ψ v)) equals the range of Dψ(v).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d r : ℕ) (N W : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P) (v : Euclid d), 1 ≤ r → IsOpen V → IsOpen W → ContDiffOn ℝ r ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ N → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → (∀ z ∈ V, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ z)) → v ∈ V → tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2 §4 (definition of T_yM for an embedded submanifold, and its identification with Dψ(ℝ^d)); used by the sibling tangential_deformation (step C2b of the parent proof) and in the chart argument of step C3c.
1. Setup. Put y := ψ(v) ∈ W ∩ N and L := Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v; since V is open and r ≥ 1, ψ is differentiable at v with derivative L. L is injective, so (finite dimension) there is c > 0 with |Lh| ≥ c|h| for all h ∈ ℝ^d; range L is a linear subspace, hence closed.
2. range L ⊆ T_yN. Let w = La. If a = 0, the constant curve γ ≡ y works (y ∈ N). Otherwise choose ρ > 0 with closedBall(v, ρ) ⊆ V and κ > 0 with κ|a| < ρ, and let σ(s) := κ·tanh(s/κ), a smooth function with σ(0) = 0, σ'(0) = 1 and |σ(s)| < κ. Put γ(s) := ψ(v + σ(s)a). Then v + σ(s)a ∈ V for all s, so γ is C^r (in particular C¹) on ℝ ⊇ (−1,1), γ(ℝ) ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ N, γ(0) = y, and γ'(0) = Dψ(v)(σ'(0)a) = La = w. Hence w ∈ T_yN.
3. Embedding property. If z_k ∈ V and ψ(z_k) → y then z_k → v: the set K := {ψ(z_k) : k} ∪ {y} is compact and contained in W, so V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) is compact and contains every z_k; any cluster point z ∈ V of (z_k) satisfies ψ(z) = y = ψ(v) by continuity, so z = v by injectivity on V; hence z_k → v.
4. T_yN ⊆ range L. Let w ∈ T_yN, witnessed by γ. As γ is continuous at 0 and W is open, there is s_0 ∈ (0,1) with γ(s) ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V) for |s| < s_0; write γ(s) = ψ(β(s)) with β(s) ∈ V (unique by injectivity). By step 3 (applied along sequences s_k → 0), β(s) → v as s → 0.
5. Write ψ(z) − y = L(z − v) + ρ(z) with |ρ(z)| ≤ η(|z − v|)·|z − v|, η(t) → 0 as t → 0. For |s| small, η(|β(s) − v|) ≤ c/2, hence |γ(s) − y| ≥ c|β(s) − v| − (c/2)|β(s) − v|, i.e. |β(s) − v| ≤ (2/c)|γ(s) − y|. Since γ is differentiable at 0, |γ(s) − y| ≤ C|s| for small |s|; thus |β(s) − v| = O(|s|) and |ρ(β(s))| = o(|s|).
6. Hence (γ(s) − y)/s = L((β(s) − v)/s) + o(1), so the difference quotients lie within o(1) of range L. Letting s → 0, w = γ'(0) belongs to the closure of range L, which is range L. Together with step 2, tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v).
proof_key_steps: Curves s ↦ ψ(v + σ(s)a) with σ smooth, bounded, σ'(0) = 1 show range Dψ(v) ⊆ T_{ψ(v)}N.
Properness and injectivity make ψ^{-1} continuous at ψ(v) along N ∩ W.
Injectivity of Dψ(v) gives |β(s) − v| = O(|γ(s) − ψ(v)|), so difference quotients of any curve in N lie in range Dψ(v) up to o(1).

subproblems.title: Deformations along a vector field tangent to a C² submanifold (Simon Ch. 2 before 5.8; Ch. 4, 2.5)
subproblems.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, N an embedded C² d-dimensional submanifold with (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and X ∈ C¹(ℝ^P; ℝ^P) with compact support, spt X ⊆ U and X(x) ∈ T_xN for x ∈ N ∩ U. Then there is a family (φ_t)_{t∈ℝ} of maps ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that every φ_t is C¹, bijective, with injective derivative everywhere, φ_t = id outside spt X and φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U, and Dφ_t = I + t·DX + o(t) uniformly: for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 with ‖Dφ_t(x) − I − t·DX(x)‖ ≤ ε|t| for all |t| < δ and all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (U N : Set (Euclid P)) (X : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ U → (∀ x ∈ N ∩ U, X x ∈ tangentSpace N x) → ∃ φ : ℝ → Euclid P → Euclid P, (∀ t, ContDiff ℝ 1 (φ t) ∧ Bijective (φ t) ∧ (∀ x, Injective (fderiv ℝ (φ t) x)) ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ tsupport X → φ t x = x) ∧ MapsTo (φ t) (N ∩ U) (N ∩ U)) ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, |t| < δ → ∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ (φ t) x - ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid P) - t • fderiv ℝ X x‖ ≤ ε * |t|
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon asserts the existence of such families in Ch. 2 (discussion before 5.8, families as in 5.6) and Ch. 4, 2.5–2.6; step C2b of the parent proof cites such a family (with φ_0 = id and initial velocity X along N). Here the family is built by composing finitely many deformations that are linear in straightening coordinates of N; it has exactly the properties used later (φ_t = id off spt X, φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U, Dφ_t = I + tDX + o(t)) and avoids differentiable dependence of ODE solutions on initial data. Write E := ℝ^P, K := tsupport X.
1. Preliminaries. Since (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, N ∩ U = N̄ ∩ U is relatively closed in U, so U ∖ N is open and K ∩ N = K ∩ N̄ is compact. By the sibling chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv), for every chart (V, W, ψ) of N (as in IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N) and v ∈ V, T_{ψ(v)}N = range Dψ(v), a linear subspace of dimension d; in particular X(z) ∈ range Dψ(v) when z = ψ(v) ∈ N ∩ U, and T_zN is closed under linear combinations.
2. Local straightening. Fix p ∈ N and a chart (V, W, ψ), ψ ∈ C²(V), with p = ψ(v_p). Let F_p := (range Dψ(v_p))^⊥ (dimension P − d) and Ψ_p(a, w) := ψ(v_p + a) + w for a ∈ V − v_p, w ∈ F_p. Ψ_p is C² and DΨ_p(0,0)(h, k) = Dψ(v_p)h + k is a linear isomorphism ℝ^d × F_p → E. By the C² inverse function theorem (Mathlib ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph, ContDiffAt.to_localInverse) there is an open product of balls B_p = B'_p × B''_p ∋ (0,0) on which Ψ_p is injective with invertible derivative, O'_p := Ψ_p(B_p) is open, and the inverse Φ_p : O'_p → B_p is C². As ψ is a homeomorphism of V onto N ∩ W (properness and injectivity, cf. step 3 of the proof of the sibling chart_tangent_space), ψ(v_p + B'_p) is a relatively open neighbourhood of p in N, so there is ρ > 0 with N ∩ B_ρ(p) ⊆ ψ(v_p + B'_p). Put O_p := O'_p ∩ B_ρ(p) ∩ U ∩ W (if p ∈ U). Then for z ∈ O_p: z ∈ N iff Φ_p(z) ∈ B'_p × {0} (if z ∈ N then z = ψ(v_p + a) = Ψ_p(a, 0) with a ∈ B'_p, and injectivity of Ψ_p on B_p gives Φ_p(z) = (a, 0); conversely Ψ_p(a, 0) = ψ(v_p + a) ∈ N).
3. Local deformations. Let Y ∈ C¹(E; E) with tsupport Y compact ⊆ O_p and Y(z) ∈ T_zN for z ∈ N ∩ O_p. Put Z(b) := DΨ_p(b)^{-1}Y(Ψ_p(b)) for b ∈ B_p and Z := 0 elsewhere; Z is C¹ (DΨ_p is C¹ and invertible on B_p) with compact support Φ_p(tsupport Y) ⊆ B_p. For b = (a, 0) ∈ B_p, Y(Ψ_p(a,0)) ∈ T_{ψ(v_p+a)}N = range Dψ(v_p + a) = DΨ_p(a,0)(ℝ^d × {0}), so Z(a, 0) ∈ ℝ^d × {0}. For |t| < t_Y := 1/(1 + sup‖DZ‖), h_t := id + tZ has ‖Dh_t − I‖ < 1 everywhere, so h_t is a C¹ diffeomorphism of ℝ^d × F_p (Mathlib ApproximatesLinearOn.toHomeomorph with the identity as linear part, plus the inverse function theorem), equal to the identity off tsupport Z; hence it maps tsupport Z and B_p onto themselves, and h_t(a, 0) = (a + tZ_1(a,0), 0) ∈ B'_p × {0} for (a, 0) ∈ B_p. Define φ^Y_t := Ψ_p∘h_t∘Φ_p on O'_p and φ^Y_t := id elsewhere. Since φ^Y_t = id on O'_p ∖ tsupport Y, φ^Y_t is C¹ on E, bijective, with invertible derivative everywhere, equal to id off tsupport Y and mapping tsupport Y ⊆ U onto itself. It maps N ∩ U into N ∩ U: for z ∈ N ∩ O_p, Φ_p(z) ∈ B'_p × {0}, so φ^Y_t(z) ∈ Ψ_p(B'_p × {0}) ⊆ N, and φ^Y_t(z) ∈ tsupport Y ∪ {z} ⊆ U; points of N outside tsupport Y are fixed. Expansion: for y ∈ O'_p and b := Φ_p(y), Dφ^Y_t(y) = DΨ_p(b + tZ(b))(I + tDZ(b))DΨ_p(b)^{-1}. Differentiating Y(Ψ_p(b)) = DΨ_p(b)Z(b) gives DY(y)DΨ_p(b) = D²Ψ_p(b)[·, Z(b)] + DΨ_p(b)DZ(b), and D²Ψ_p is symmetric and uniformly continuous on a compact neighbourhood of tsupport Z, so DΨ_p(b + tZ(b)) = DΨ_p(b) + tD²Ψ_p(b)[Z(b), ·] + o(t) uniformly in b ∈ tsupport Z. Multiplying out, Dφ^Y_t(y) = I + tDY(y) + o(t) uniformly in y ∈ tsupport Y; for y ∉ tsupport Y both sides equal I (φ^Y_t = id near y, DY(y) = 0). Thus sup_y ‖Dφ^Y_t(y) − I − tDY(y)‖ = o(t), and |φ^Y_t(y) − y| ≤ C_Y|t| for all y.
4. Partition of unity. Cover the compact K ∩ N by finitely many O_{p_1}, …, O_{p_m} (p_i ∈ K ∩ N ⊆ U) and put O_0 := U ∖ N (open); then K ⊆ O_0 ∪ O_{p_1} ∪ ⋯ ∪ O_{p_m}. Choose smooth χ_0, …, χ_m with compact tsupport χ_i ⊆ O_{p_i} (tsupport χ_0 ⊆ O_0) and Σ_i χ_i = 1 on a neighbourhood of K (smooth partition of unity subordinate to a finite open cover of a compact set; Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity / exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset). Put X_i := χ_i X. Then X = Σ_i X_i, X_i ∈ C¹_c with tsupport X_i ⊆ tsupport χ_i ∩ K; for i ≥ 1, X_i(z) = χ_i(z)X(z) ∈ T_zN for z ∈ N ∩ O_{p_i}; and X_0 = 0 on N.
5. The family. Let φ^0_t := id + tX_0 and φ^i_t := φ^{X_i}_t (step 3 with p = p_i), and t_0 := min(t_{X_1}, …, t_{X_m}, 1/(1 + sup‖DX_0‖)) > 0. For |t| < t_0 set φ_t := φ^0_t∘φ^1_t∘⋯∘φ^m_t, and φ_t := id for |t| ≥ t_0. For every t: (a) φ_t is C¹, bijective, with invertible (in particular injective) derivative everywhere (φ^0_t by the argument of step 3, compositions of such maps); (b) φ_t(x) = x for x ∉ K, because each factor is the identity outside tsupport X_i ⊆ K; (c) φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U, because each φ^i_t (i ≥ 1) maps N ∩ U into itself and φ^0_t fixes every point of N. (d) Expansion: with y_i := φ^{i+1}_t∘⋯∘φ^m_t(x), Dφ_t(x) = Dφ^0_t(y_0)·Dφ^1_t(y_1)⋯Dφ^m_t(x); each factor is I + tDX_i(y_i) + o(t) uniformly (step 3; exact for i = 0), |y_i − x| ≤ C|t|, and the DX_i are uniformly continuous, so DX_i(y_i) = DX_i(x) + o(1) uniformly. Multiplying the finitely many bounded factors, Dφ_t(x) = I + tΣ_i DX_i(x) + o(t) = I + tDX(x) + o(t) uniformly in x: for every ε > 0 there is δ ∈ (0, t_0] with ‖Dφ_t(x) − I − tDX(x)‖ ≤ ε|t| for all |t| < δ and all x.
proof_key_steps: Straighten N near each point by the C² map (a, w) ↦ ψ(v_p + a) + w and the inverse function theorem.
In straightening coordinates a field tangent to N is horizontal on ℝ^d × {0}, so b ↦ b + tZ(b) preserves N; conjugating gives C¹ diffeomorphisms with Dφ_t = I + tDY + o(t).
A partition of unity splits X into finitely many such pieces plus a piece vanishing on N; composing the deformations gives the family.

subproblems.title: Uniform mean-curvature bound and monotonicity for varifolds stationary in N (Simon Ch. 4, 2.7 and 3.17)
subproblems.statement: Let ℓ ≤ k and n ≥ 1, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^{n+k} with (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and y₀ ∈ N ∩ U. There exist r₀ > 0 and κ ≥ 0 with B̄_{3r₀}(y₀) ⊆ U such that, for every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every integer multiplicity triple R = (M, θ, ξ) representing T with spt T ⊆ N and V = v(M, θ) stationary in U ∩ N (δV(X) = 0 for every C¹ vector field X with compact support, spt X ⊆ U and X(x) ∈ T_xN for all x ∈ N ∩ U), the following hold: (a) there is a μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable H : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ^{n+k} with |H(x)| ≤ κ for all x and δV(X) = −∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ_R for every C¹ vector field X with compact support contained in B_{2r₀}(y₀); (b) for every z ∈ B_{r₀}(y₀) and 0 < σ ≤ ρ ≤ r₀, e^{κσ}σ^{−n}μ_R(B_σ(z)) ≤ e^{κρ}ρ^{−n}μ_R(B_ρ(z)). Here μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M, δV(X) = ∫_M θ div_M X dHⁿ (IMRep.firstVariation) with div_M X(x) = trace(P_{T_xM}∘DX(x)), T_xN is the classical tangent space (tangentSpace), and r₀, κ depend only on n, N, U, y₀.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step C3 of the parent proof, localized at a point y₀ ∈ N ∩ U (the parent applies it with y₀ := x); Simon Ch. 4, 2.5–2.7 (chapter-04.txt lines 157–210: if V is stationary in U ∩ N then ∫div_M X dμ_V = −∫X·H̄_N dμ_V with H̄_N = Σ_i B_x(τ_i, τ_i)) and Ch. 4, 3.3–3.6, 3.14–3.17 (chapter-04.txt lines 255–320 and 370–430: monotonicity with bounded mean curvature). Uses the sibling mass_support (Submission.dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support). Notation: T_xM is the approximate tangent space, which where it exists equals approxTangentPlane n M x (uniqueness); for an orthonormal basis τ of T_xM, div_M X(x) = Σ_i⟨τ_i, DX(x)τ_i⟩ = tangentialDivergence; P(q) denotes the orthogonal projection onto T_qN.
1. Local geometry of N and the constants. Let (V₀, W₀, ψ) be a chart of N at y₀ from IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+ℓ) N: ψ is C², injective, proper onto W₀ ∩ N = ψ(V₀), with injective differential. Hence N ∩ W₀ is an embedded C² submanifold, T_qN = Dψ(v)(ℝ^{n+ℓ}) for q = ψ(v) (C¹ curves in N ∩ W₀ lift through a local C¹ inverse of ψ), and q ↦ P(q) is C¹ along N ∩ W₀ (P(ψ(v)) = Dψ(v)(Dψ(v)ᵀDψ(v))⁻¹Dψ(v)ᵀ). Choose r_a > 0 with B̄_{8r_a}(y₀) ⊆ U ∩ W₀. Because (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, N ∩ B̄_{8r_a}(y₀) = N̄ ∩ B̄_{8r_a}(y₀) is compact. By the tubular neighbourhood theorem for C² submanifolds (R. L. Foote, Proc. AMS 92 (1984) 153–155; G. Leobacher and A. Steinicke, Ann. Global Anal. Geom. 60 (2021) 559–587, arXiv:1811.10578: the nearest point projection onto a C^k submanifold is C^{k−1} near it), after decreasing r_a every x ∈ B_{4r_a}(y₀) has a unique nearest point π(x) ∈ N (it lies in N ∩ B_{8r_a}(y₀) because dist(x, N) ≤ |x − y₀|), π : B_{4r_a}(y₀) → N is C¹, π(q) = q and Dπ(q) = P(q) for q ∈ N ∩ B_{4r_a}(y₀). Then Π := P∘π is C¹ on B_{4r_a}(y₀) and Π = P on N ∩ B_{4r_a}(y₀). For q ∈ N ∩ B_{4r_a}(y₀) and u, v ∈ T_qN put B_q(u, v) := (D_uP)(q)v (derivative of P along N). Differentiating P² = P shows P(q)(D_uP)(q)u = 0, so B_q(u, u) ⊥ T_qN; and |B_q(u, v)| ≤ β|u||v| with β := sup ‖DP‖ over N ∩ B̄_{4r_a}(y₀) < ∞ (continuity on a compact set). Set r₀ := r_a and κ := nβ; then B̄_{3r₀}(y₀) ⊆ U.
2. M ⊆ N up to a null set. Fix T, R as in the statement. By mass_support (ii), spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R. As μ_R(ℝ^{n+k} ∖ spt μ_R) = 0 (second countability; Mathlib Measure.measure_compl_support) and μ_R(ℝ^{n+k} ∖ U) = 0 (M ⊆ U), μ_R(ℝ^{n+k} ∖ spt T) = 0; with spt T ⊆ N this gives μ_R(ℝ^{n+k} ∖ N) = 0, i.e. Hⁿ(M ∖ N) = 0 (θ ≥ 1 on M).
3. Approximate tangent spaces lie in T_xN. Let G₀ be the set of x ∈ M ∩ N at which T_xM exists and is oriented by ξ(x) (R.orients); Hⁿ(M ∖ G₀) = 0 by step 2. Let x ∈ G₀ ∩ B_{4r₀}(y₀) and v ∈ T_xM with |v| = 1. Since Hⁿ⌞(M ∖ N) = 0, the blow-ups of Hⁿ⌞M at x are those of Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ N). For each s ∈ (0, 1/2), the sets η_{x,λ}(M ∩ N) meet B_s(v) for all small λ > 0: otherwise, along some λ_i ↓ 0, ∫_{η_{x,λ_i}(M)} f dHⁿ = 0 for an f ∈ C_c(B_s(v)) with f ≥ 0, f(v) > 0, contradicting convergence to ∫_{T_xM} f dHⁿ > 0. So v = lim (x_i − x)/λ_i with x_i ∈ M ∩ N, x_i → x, |x_i − x|/λ_i → 1. Since N ∩ W₀ is a C¹ submanifold, the unit vectors (x_i − x)/|x_i − x| accumulate only in T_xN; hence v ∈ T_xN, and T_xM ⊆ T_xN.
4. Definition of H. For x ∈ G₀ ∩ B_{4r₀}(y₀) let H(x) := Σ_{i=1}^n B_x(τ_i, τ_i) for an orthonormal basis τ of T_xM ⊆ T_xN. This does not depend on the basis, since it equals Σ_{a,b}(P_{T_xM})_{ab}·B_x(P(x)e_a, P(x)e_b). Put H(x) := 0 at all other points. Then |H(x)| ≤ nβ = κ for every x. H is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable: P_{T_xM} = Σ_i τ_iτ_iᵀ is a continuous function of the unit simple n-vector ξ(x) = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ (the sign cancels), ξ is a.e. strongly measurable, and x ↦ B_x is continuous on N ∩ B̄_{4r₀}(y₀).
5. First variation formula (a) (Simon 2.7). Let X be C¹ with compact support, spt X ⊆ B_{2r₀}(y₀). Define X^T(x) := Π(x)X(x) for x ∈ B_{4r₀}(y₀) and X^T(x) := 0 otherwise. X^T is C¹: it is C¹ on the open set B_{4r₀}(y₀), it vanishes on the open set ℝ^{n+k} ∖ spt X, and these two open sets cover ℝ^{n+k}. Its support lies in spt X, a compact subset of U, and X^T(x) ∈ T_xN for every x ∈ N ∩ U (X^T(x) = P(x)X(x) if x ∈ N ∩ B_{4r₀}(y₀), and X^T(x) = 0 otherwise). Stationarity (R.IsStationaryAlong N) gives δV(X^T) = 0. Let Y := X − X^T, which equals (I − Π)X on B_{4r₀}(y₀). Let x ∈ G₀ ∩ B_{4r₀}(y₀), and let τ be an orthonormal basis of T_xM ⊆ T_xN. Then DY(x)τ_i = −(DΠ(x)τ_i)X(x) + (I − P(x))DX(x)τ_i. We have ⟨τ_i, (I − P(x))w⟩ = 0 for all w. Also DΠ(x)τ_i = DP(x)[Dπ(x)τ_i] = (D_{τ_i}P)(x), because Dπ(x) = P(x) is the identity on T_xN. Since (D_{τ_i}P)(x) is symmetric, ⟨τ_i, (D_{τ_i}P)(x)X(x)⟩ = ⟨B_x(τ_i, τ_i), X(x)⟩. Hence div_M Y(x) = −⟨X(x), H(x)⟩. The same identity holds at μ_R-a.e. x outside B_{4r₀}(y₀): there X and Y vanish near x, so both sides are 0. The integrands θ·div_M X^T and θ·div_M Y are bounded and vanish off the compact set spt X, so δV is additive on them and δV(X) = δV(X^T) + δV(Y) = −∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ_R. This proves (a).
6. Monotonicity (b) (Simon 3.3–3.6, 3.16–3.17). Fix z ∈ B_{r₀}(y₀) and R_z with r₀ < R_z < 2r₀ − |z − y₀|, so B̄_{R_z}(z) ⊆ B_{2r₀}(y₀). Let g : ℝ → [0, 1] be C¹ and nondecreasing with g = 0 on (−∞, 0] and g = 1 on [1, ∞). For ε ∈ (0, 1) let γ_ε(t) := g((1 − t)/ε): γ_ε is C¹ and nonincreasing, γ_ε = 1 on (−∞, 1 − ε], γ_ε = 0 on [1, ∞), and γ_ε increases to the indicator of (−∞, 1) as ε ↓ 0. With r(x) := |x − z| and s ∈ (0, R_z), the field X_s(x) := γ_ε(r/s)(x − z) is C¹ (γ_ε(r/s) is constant near z) and spt X_s ⊆ B̄_s(z) ⊆ B_{2r₀}(y₀). At μ_R-a.e. x, div_M X_s = nγ_ε(r/s) + (r/s)γ_ε'(r/s)(1 − |∇^⊥r|²), where ∇^⊥r is the component of ∇r orthogonal to T_xM. Let I(s) := ∫γ_ε(r/s) dμ_R and J(s) := ∫γ_ε(r/s)|∇^⊥r|² dμ_R. These are finite and, by dominated convergence, differentiable in s, with sI'(s) = −∫(r/s)γ_ε'(r/s) dμ_R and sJ'(s) = −∫(r/s)γ_ε'(r/s)|∇^⊥r|² dμ_R ≥ 0. By (a), nI(s) − sI'(s) + sJ'(s) = δV(X_s) = −∫γ_ε(r/s)⟨x − z, H⟩ dμ_R. Hence (s^{−n}I)'(s) = s^{−n−1}(sJ'(s) + ∫γ_ε(r/s)⟨x − z, H⟩ dμ_R) ≥ −κ s^{−n}I(s), because J' ≥ 0 and |⟨x − z, H⟩| ≤ κs on the support of γ_ε(r/s). Therefore (e^{κs}s^{−n}I(s))' ≥ 0 on (0, R_z), and e^{κσ}σ^{−n}I(σ) ≤ e^{κρ}ρ^{−n}I(ρ) for 0 < σ ≤ ρ ≤ r₀. Letting ε ↓ 0, I(s) increases to μ_R(B_s(z)) (monotone convergence). This gives (b) in [0, ∞]; both sides are finite because B̄_ρ(z) is a compact subset of U. (Equivalently, apply SimonGMT Chapter04/MeanCurvature.lean, HasGeneralizedMeanCurvatureIn.exp_normalizedBallMass_monotoneOn, for closed balls and take left limits.)
proof_key_steps: Choose a C² chart and a C¹ nearest point retraction π near y₀; fix the second fundamental form bound β and set κ = nβ.
By the support identity, μ_R is carried by spt T ⊆ N, and a.e. approximate tangent space lies inside T_xN.
Split X = Π X + (I − Π)X: stationarity kills the tangential part, and the normal part gives div_M = −⟨X, H⟩ with H = Σ B(τ_i, τ_i), |H| ≤ κ.
The radial first variation with |H| ≤ κ makes e^{κs}s^{−n}μ_R(B_s(z)) nondecreasing.

subproblems.title: Simon 6.2.23–2.24 and 6.3.3–3.9: push-forward of an integer multiplicity current by a C¹ diffeomorphism
subproblems.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple representing T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), K ⊆ U compact, and φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P a C¹ bijection with Dφ(x) injective for every x and φ(x) = x for x ∉ K. Then there is an integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with S(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(φ^#ω(x)) dH^n(x) for all ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), where φ^#ω(x) = ω(φ(x))∘Dφ(x) is the pulled-back covector (so S = φ_#T), and ∂S = 0 whenever ∂T = 0 (BoundaryVanishes; vacuous for n = 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n) (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → Bijective φ → (∀ x, Injective (fderiv ℝ φ x)) → (∀ x, x ∉ K → φ x = x) → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n, IsIntegerMultiplicity S ∧ (BoundaryVanishes T → BoundaryVanishes S) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = ∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (φ x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ φ x)) ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 6.2.23–2.24 (definition of f_#T, ∂f_# = f_#∂, the integral formula 2.24(2)–(3)) and 6.3.3–3.9 (f_#T is integer multiplicity; for injective f, f_#T = τ(f(M), θ∘f^{-1}, induced orientation), with the induced orientation of 3.5/3.7), together with Ch. 3 §1–2 (approximate tangent planes, area formula); this is the competitor S_t = φ_{t#}T of step C2c of the parent proof, used through the sibling stationary_of_minimizing. The printed argument (3.6–3.7) uses without proof that dφ_x maps T_xM onto the approximate tangent plane of φ(M) at φ(x) for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M; steps 4–6 supply this. Notation: E := ℝ^P; M, θ, ξ from R; Q(x) := approxTangentPlane n M x and p(x) its orthogonal projection; for a linear L and a plane Q, J(L, Q) := normDet(L restricted to Q) = (det(Lτ_a·Lτ_b))^{1/2} for any orthonormal basis τ of Q (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet, normDet_sq_eq_det_gram); β∘L denotes β.compContinuousLinearMap L. The argument is uniform in n ≥ 0; step 10 records what each step reduces to when n = 0.
1. φ is a bi-Lipschitz C¹ diffeomorphism preserving U. By the inverse function theorem φ^{-1} is C¹ (Dφ(x) is an injective, hence invertible, endomorphism of E). φ is the identity on the open set E ∖ K, so Dφ = I there, φ(E ∖ K) = E ∖ K, hence (φ bijective) φ(K) = K, φ(U) = U and φ^{-1}(U) = U. Dφ − I and D(φ^{-1}) − I are continuous with compact support, so ‖Dφ‖, ‖D(φ^{-1})‖ ≤ Λ on E for some Λ ≥ 1 and, by the mean value inequality, φ and φ^{-1} are Λ-Lipschitz. Hence Λ^{-n}H^n(A) ≤ H^n(φ(A)) ≤ Λ^n H^n(A) for all A ⊆ E (Mathlib LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le for φ and φ^{-1}; μHE[n] is a fixed positive multiple of μH[n]); in particular φ and φ^{-1} map H^n-null sets to H^n-null sets.
2. S is a current with the stated action. For ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) let g_ω(x) := θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(φx)∘Dφ(x)). For a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x)(β) = ±β(τ) with |τ_i| = 1, so |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ (operator norm), and ‖β∘L‖ ≤ ‖β‖‖L‖^n. g_ω vanishes off C_ω := φ^{-1}(tsupport ω), a compact subset of U, so |g_ω| ≤ Λ^n·sup‖ω‖·θ·1_{C_ω} a.e. on M, which is integrable by R.locallyIntegrable_mult; g_ω is a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable, ξ a.e. strongly measurable, x ↦ ω(φx) and x ↦ Dφ(x) continuous, evaluation continuous). Define S(ω) := ∫_M g_ω dH^n. S is linear in ω, and if ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in one compact C ⊆ U, uniform convergence) then |S(ω_j)| ≤ Λ^n sup‖ω_j‖ ∫_{M∩φ^{-1}C} θ dH^n → 0; so S is a GeometricCurrentOn U n with the required action formula.
3. Boundary. Let n ≥ 1 and T.boundary = 0 (for n = 0, BoundaryVanishes S is True). Fix η ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(U). Let ρ_k be smooth mollifiers supported in B_{1/k}(0) and φ_k := id + ρ_k∗(φ − id). Then φ_k is C^∞, φ_k = id outside K_k := K + closedBall(0, 1/k), a compact subset of U for k ≥ k_0, and φ_k → φ, Dφ_k → Dφ uniformly on E. The pulled-back form φ_k^#η(x) := η(φ_k x)∘Dφ_k(x) is smooth with tsupport ⊆ tsupport η ∪ K_k (φ_k = id near every point outside K_k), so φ_k^#η ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(U), and d(φ_k^#η) = φ_k^#(dη) (exterior derivative commutes with pull-back by smooth maps: SimonGMT exteriorDerivativeOn_pullbackFormWithin with domains univ, i.e. Mathlib extDerivWithin_pullback). Therefore 0 = T.boundary(φ_k^#η) = T(φ_k^#dη) = ∫_M θ ξ(dη(φ_k x)∘Dφ_k(x)) dH^n. As k → ∞ these integrands converge pointwise to θ ξ(dη(φx)∘Dφ(x)) and are dominated by C·θ·1_{tsupport η ∪ K_{k_0}}; by dominated convergence S(dη) = 0. So S.boundary = 0.
4. Lipschitz pieces of M. By R.rectifiable (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable n M) there are M_0 ⊆ E with H^n(M_0) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^n → E (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M_0 ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n). Let G_j := {a ∈ ℝ^n : F_j is differentiable at a and DF_j(a) is injective} (SimonGMT areaRegularSet F_j); G_j is Borel (SimonGMT measurableSet_areaRegularSet) and H^n(F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j)) = 0 (SimonGMT area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero).
 (a) Coercivity constant. For an injective linear map A : ℝ^n → E define m(A) > 0 as follows. If n ≥ 1, m(A) := min{|Ah| : h ∈ ℝ^n, |h| = 1}; the minimum exists and is positive because the unit sphere of ℝ^n is compact and nonempty and h ↦ |Ah| is continuous and nowhere zero on it. If n = 0, m(A) := 1; the unit sphere of ℝ^0 = {0} is empty, so no minimum is taken. In both cases (†) |Ah| ≥ m(A)|h| for every h ∈ ℝ^n: for n ≥ 1 and h ≠ 0 apply the definition to h/|h| and multiply by |h|; for h = 0, which is the only vector when n = 0, both sides vanish. (Alternatively, one may take m(A) := 1/K for any K > 0 with AntilipschitzWith K A, which Mathlib's LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith supplies for every injective A in every dimension, including n = 0; only m(A) > 0 and (†) are used below.)
 (b) Positive radius. Define r : (ℝ^n →L[ℝ] E) → ℝ≥0 by r(A) := m(A)/2 if A is injective and r(A) := 1 otherwise. Then r(A) > 0, hence r(A) ≠ 0, for every A, including every A when n = 0 (then every A is injective and r(A) = 1/2). This is exactly the hypothesis rpos : ∀ A, r A ≠ 0 of Mathlib's exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.1.2 and its proof (chapter-07.txt lines 29–60) with README erratum 1, i.e. step C2 of the parent proof (Simon 7.1.2, first claim); in the parent the hypothesis H^n(M ∖ N) = 0 is obtained in step C1e from spt T ⊆ N and the sibling carrier_support_null. Siblings used: mass_support (MASS; Submission.dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support, whose first conjunct gives T.massOn W = R.measure W for every open W), diffeo_pushforward (PUSH; Submission.codim1_ldr_imrep_c1_diffeo_pushforward_im), tangential_deformation (DEFORM; Submission.tangential_c1_deformation_exists), first_variation_mass_bound (EXPAND; Submission.codim1_ldr_pushforward_massOn_le_first_variation).
1. Fix X ∈ C¹(ℝ^P; ℝ^P) with compact support, tsupport X ⊆ U and X(x) ∈ tangentSpace N x for x ∈ N ∩ U. Put K := tsupport X (compact, ⊆ U) and δV(X) := R.firstVariation X = ∫_M θ div_M X dH^n. We show δV(X) = 0.
2. Case n = 0. approxTangentPlane 0 M x has finrank 0, hence equals ⊥, for every x (in both branches of its definition), so its projection is 0 and tangentialDivergence 0 M X x = trace 0 = 0; thus δV(X) = 0. Assume n ≥ 1 from now on.
3. Choice of W. As K is compact in the open U, there is an open W with K ⊆ W, closure W compact and closure W ⊆ U (a small open thickening of K). Then R.measure W ≤ ∫_{M∩closure W} θ dH^n < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult), and by MASS (first conjunct, W open), T.massOn W = R.measure W. Put m := (R.measure W).toReal, so R.measure W = ofReal m.
4. Degenerate case m = 0. Then H^n(M ∩ W) = 0 (θ ≥ 1 on M). For x ∉ K, DX(x) = 0 (X vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K), so tangentialDivergence n M X x = 0. Hence the integrand of δV(X) vanishes H^n⌞M-a.e. and δV(X) = 0. Assume m > 0.
5. Deformations. DEFORM (applied to U, N, X) gives φ : ℝ → ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that for every t: φ_t is C¹, bijective, with injective derivative, φ_t = id off K and φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U; and (D): for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 with ‖Dφ_t(x) − I − tDX(x)‖ ≤ ε|t| for all |t| < δ and all x. Since φ_t is a bijection fixing every point of ℝ^P ∖ K, it maps ℝ^P ∖ K onto itself and hence K onto K.
6. Competitors. For each t, PUSH (with U, T, R, K and φ_t) gives an integer multiplicity S_t ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with BoundaryVanishes S_t (because BoundaryVanishes T) and S_t(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω(φ_t x)∘Dφ_t(x)) dH^n for all ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U).
7. S_t is admissible in 7.1.1 with this W. (a) W is open and CompactlyContained W U; S_t is integer multiplicity. (b) SameBoundary S_t T: n ≥ 1 and S_t.boundary = 0 = T.boundary. (c) spt(S_t − T) ⊆ K ∩ N. K ∩ N is compact: N ∩ U = N̄ ∩ U by (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, so K ∩ N = K ∩ N̄ is closed in the compact K. Let y ∈ U ∖ (K ∩ N); choose r > 0 with closedBall(y, r) ⊆ U and closedBall(y, r) ∩ K ∩ N = ∅, and W_y := ball(y, r) (open, closure compact ⊆ U). For ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W_y, using T ω = R.action ω: (S_t − T)(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)[ξ(x)(ω(φ_t x)∘Dφ_t(x)) − ξ(x)(ω(x))] dH^n; the two integrals may be merged because both integrands are integrable (each is a.e. strongly measurable and bounded by C·θ on a compact subset of U — φ_t^{-1}(tsupport ω), resp. tsupport ω — and vanishes elsewhere, |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ a.e.; R.locallyIntegrable_mult). The bracket vanishes for x ∈ M ∖ K (φ_t = id on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K, so φ_t x = x and Dφ_t(x) = I); it vanishes for x ∈ M ∩ K ∩ N, because x and φ_t(x) both lie in K ∩ N (step 5: φ_t(K) = K, φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U) where ω vanishes; and M ∩ K ∖ N is H^n-null by hypothesis. So S_t − T vanishes on W_y and y ∈ zeroRegion(S_t − T). Hence spt(S_t − T) ⊆ K ∩ N ⊆ (N ∩ U) ∩ W. (d) spt(S_t − T) is compact: it is relatively closed in U (complement of the open zeroRegion) and contained in the compact set K ∩ N ⊆ U, so it equals (K ∩ N) ∩ F for a closed F.
   Therefore IsMinimizingIn T (N ∩ U) gives T.massOn W ≤ S_t.massOn W, i.e. ofReal m ≤ S_t.massOn W, for every t ∈ ℝ.
8. First variation bound. EXPAND (with W open, R.measure W ≠ ∞, X C¹ with compact support, K ⊆ W, φ_t C¹, φ_t = id off K, and (D)) gives: for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that S_t.massOn W ≤ ofReal(m + t·δV(X) + ε|t|) for all |t| < δ (S_t satisfies the action formula required there).
9. Conclusion. Suppose a := δV(X) ≠ 0. Take ε := |a|/2, δ from step 8, and t := −s·sign(a) with 0 < s < δ and s|a|/2 < m. Then m + ta + ε|t| = m − s|a|/2 ∈ (0, m), and steps 7–8 give ofReal m ≤ S_t.massOn W ≤ ofReal(m − s|a|/2) < ofReal m, a contradiction. Hence δV(X) = R.firstVariation X = 0. As X was arbitrary, R.IsStationaryAlong N.
proof_key_steps: n = 0 is trivial (0-dimensional approximate tangent planes); otherwise fix X tangent to N and W ⊂⊂ U containing spt X, with M_W(T) = μ_V(W).
The deformations φ_t (DEFORM) push T forward to integer multiplicity competitors S_t (PUSH) with ∂S_t = 0 and spt(S_t − T) ⊆ spt X ∩ N compact, using H^n(M ∖ N) = 0.
Minimality gives μ_V(W) ≤ M_W(S_t) ≤ μ_V(W) + tδV(X) + ε|t| (EXPAND) for all small t of both signs, forcing δV(X) = 0.

subproblems.title: Allard regularity for integer multiplicity varifolds with bounded mean curvature (graph form)
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and k ≥ 0. For every ε > 0 there are δ₀ > 0 and γ ∈ (0, 1] with the following property. Let U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} be any set, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep) with weight μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure), W ⊆ U open, κ ∈ ℝ, ρ > 0, z ∈ ℝ^{n+k}, and H : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ^{n+k} μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable with |H(x)| ≤ κ for all x, such that v(M, θ) has generalized mean curvature H in W: R.firstVariation X = ∫_M θ div_M X dHⁿ = −∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ_R for every C¹ compactly supported vector field X with tsupport X ⊆ W (div_M X(x) = trace(p_{T_xM}∘DX(x)), T_xM the approximate tangent plane of M). If the closed ball B̄_ρ(z) ⊆ W, z ∈ spt μ_R, μ_R(B̄_ρ(z)) ≤ (1 + δ₀)ω_nρⁿ and κρ ≤ δ₀, then there are linear isometries ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{n+k} with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w, and u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k with u(0) = 0, u of class C¹ on the open ball B_{γρ}(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ with ‖Du(v)‖ ≤ ε there, such that spt μ_R ∩ B_{γρ}(z) = {z + ιv + ι'u(v) : |v| < γρ} ∩ B_{γρ}(z) (open balls). This is Allard's Regularity Theorem (Simon Ch. 5, 5.2 with Remark 5.3) for integer multiplicity varifolds with bounded generalized mean curvature, i.e. the case p = 2n of hypotheses 5.1.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Role in the parent proof: this is the Allard Regularity Theorem (Simon Ch. 5, 5.2) cited in steps C0 and C4–C5, in the bounded-mean-curvature form p = 2n; the parent applies it with ε := 1/2 and δ := δ₀/2. Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 5 §§2–5, the proof of the Allard Regularity Theorem 5.2 (chapter-05.txt lines 1008–1032 for 5.1–5.2; Lemma 2.1, Remark 2.2, (2.3)–(2.4), Affine Approximation 2.5, Lipschitz Approximation 2.6, Corollary 2.7, Harmonic Approximation 3.1–3.4, Tilt-excess Decay 4.5–4.6 and the proof of 5.2, printed pp. 106–124), with the monotonicity identity of Ch. 4, 3.3–3.17 (chapter-04.txt lines 215–455). The printed proof is copied with p := 2n and bounded mean curvature: since |H| ≤ κ, each term ρ^{1−n/p}(∫_{B_ρ}|H|^p dμ)^{1/p} of Simon is at most C(n)κρ, so Simon's smallness hypothesis on H is replaced by κρ ≤ δ, Simon's E_* by E_*(ξ, r, S) := max{E(ξ, r, S), δ^{−1}κ²r²}, Simon's decay exponent 2(1 − n/p) equals 1, and the bounded-H monotonicity 3.17 replaces 4.7. Departures from the printed text are marked Correction.

Notation. E := ℝ^{n+k}; B_t(x) is the closed ball, B̆_t(x) the open ball (Lean ball); Bⁿ, B̆ⁿ denote balls in ℝⁿ or in an n-plane; ω_n := unitBallVolume n. M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult (a positive integer on M), μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M with Hⁿ := μHE[n]. Since W ⊆ U is open and IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult holds on compact subsets of U, μ and Hⁿ⌞M are finite on compact subsets of W. For Hⁿ-a.e. (hence μ-a.e.) x ∈ M the approximate tangent plane T_xM := approxTangentPlane n M x exists and is n-dimensional (IMRep.orients); p_x is the orthogonal projection onto T_xM and p_x^⊥ := I − p_x. For an n-plane S, p_S and p_S^⊥ := I − p_S. |A| is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm and ‖A‖ ≤ |A| the operator norm. div_M X(x) := trace(p_x∘DX(x)), so R.firstVariation X = ∫ div_M X dμ. The hypothesis is (MC): ∫ div_M X dμ = −∫ X·H dμ for every C¹ compactly supported X : E → E with tsupport X ⊆ W; and |H| ≤ κ everywhere (so κ ≥ 0). Tilt-excess (Simon 4.1): E(ξ, r, S) := r^{−n}∫_{B_r(ξ)}|p_x − p_S|² dμ(x). α := 1/(2n+2). No translation, dilation or rotation of R is used: balls have arbitrary centres and rotations are only choices of orthonormal coordinates. For readability we write z = 0 (read B_t(y) as B_t(z + y)).

Part 0. Constants.
0.1 Fix c₀ = c₀(n, k) ∈ (0, 1/4] as in 8.6 and put L₀ := min{ε, c₀}.
0.2 Parts 2–8 introduce finitely many smallness thresholds for δ, each depending only on n, k and L₀; δ_A ∈ (0, 1/8] denotes their minimum. We prove (★): if δ := δ_A and (SA) below holds for some ρ > 0, then there are an n-plane T₀ and a map f : T₀ → T₀^⊥, C¹ on A := {v ∈ T₀ : |v| < δρ/16} with ‖Df‖ ≤ L₀ there and f(0) = 0, such that spt μ ∩ B̆_{δρ/16}(0) = {v + f(v) : v ∈ A} ∩ B̆_{δρ/16}(0). Part 9 derives the Lean statement with δ₀ := δ_A and γ := δ_A/16.

Part 1. Monotonicity and densities (Simon Ch. 4, 3.3–3.17, 4.10; Ch. 3, 1.5).
1.1 Let y ∈ E, R > 0 with B_R(y) ⊆ W, r := |x − y|, D^⊥r(x) := p_x^⊥((x − y)/r). Then for 0 < s < t < R:
 (M1) ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_s(y)} r^{−n}|D^⊥r|² dμ ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) − e^{κs}s^{−n}μ(B_s(y));
 (M2) e^{−κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) − e^{−κs}s^{−n}μ(B_s(y)) ≤ ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_s(y)} r^{−n}|D^⊥r|² dμ.
 Here r^{−n}|D^⊥r|² = |x − y|^{−n−2}|p_x^⊥(x − y)|².
 Proof (Simon 3.2–3.6, 3.16–3.17). Let ε' ∈ (0, 1) with (1+ε')t < R and φ ∈ C¹(ℝ) with 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ' ≤ 0, φ ≡ 1 on (−∞, 1], φ ≡ 0 on [1+ε', ∞). For τ ∈ (0, t] let X_τ(x) := φ(r/τ)(x − y); it is C¹ (it equals x − y near y) with tsupport in B_{(1+ε')τ}(y) ⊆ W. At μ-a.e. x, DX_τ = φ(r/τ)I + τ^{−1}φ'(r/τ)(x − y)⊗∇r, so div_M X_τ = nφ(r/τ) + (r/τ)φ'(r/τ)(1 − |D^⊥r|²), because trace p_x = n and p_x∇r·∇r = 1 − |D^⊥r|². With I(τ) := ∫φ(r/τ)dμ and J(τ) := ∫φ(r/τ)|D^⊥r|²dμ (C¹ in τ by differentiation under the integral) and (r/τ)φ'(r/τ) = −τ∂_τ[φ(r/τ)], (MC) gives nI(τ) − τI'(τ) + τJ'(τ) = −h(τ), where h(τ) := ∫φ(r/τ)(x − y)·H dμ and |h(τ)| ≤ (1+ε')κτI(τ). Thus g(τ) := τ^{−n}I(τ) satisfies g' = τ^{−n}J' + e with |e| ≤ cg, c := (1+ε')κ; as J' ≥ 0, (e^{cτ}g)' ≥ τ^{−n}J' and (e^{−cτ}g)' ≤ τ^{−n}J'. Integrating over [s, t]: ∫_s^t τ^{−n}J' dτ ≤ e^{ct}g(t) − e^{cs}g(s) and e^{−ct}g(t) − e^{−cs}g(s) ≤ ∫_s^t τ^{−n}J' dτ. By Fubini (Simon 3.5), ∫_s^t τ^{−n}J'(τ)dτ = ∫|D^⊥r|²(∫_s^t τ^{−n}∂_τφ(r/τ)dτ)dμ, and the inner integral lies between r^{−n}(φ(r/t) − φ(r/s)) and (1+ε')ⁿr^{−n}(φ(r/t) − φ(r/s)); moreover 1_{B_t∖B_{(1+ε')s}} ≤ φ(r/t) − φ(r/s) ≤ 1_{B_{(1+ε')t}∖B_s} and μ(B_τ(y)) ≤ I(τ) ≤ μ(B_{(1+ε')τ}(y)). Letting ε' ↓ 0 (closed balls decrease to closed balls) gives (M1) and (M2).
1.2 Consequences. (a) τ ↦ e^{κτ}τ^{−n}μ(B_τ(y)) is nondecreasing on (0, R) (cf. library HasGeneralizedMeanCurvatureIn.exp_normalizedBallMass_monotoneOn). (b) Θ(μ, y) := lim_{τ↓0} μ(B_τ(y))/(ω_nτⁿ) exists in [0, ∞) for every y ∈ W. (c) For 0 < t < R: ∫_{B_t(y)} |x − y|^{−n−2}|p_x^⊥(x − y)|² dμ ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) − ω_nΘ(μ, y) (let s ↓ 0 in (M1); μ({y}) = 0 as n ≥ 1). (d) If μ(B_s(y)) = 0 then μ(B_t(y)) ≤ e^{κt}tⁿ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_s(y)} |x − y|^{−n−2}|p_x^⊥(x − y)|² dμ (by (M2)).
1.3 Θ(μ, y) ≥ 1 for y ∈ spt μ ∩ W (Simon Ch. 4, 4.10(1)). (i) If x ∈ M and T_xM exists, then Hⁿ(M ∩ B_τ(x))/(ω_nτⁿ) → 1 (Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(3): test the definition of the approximate tangent plane with continuous compactly supported functions squeezed between the indicators of B_{1−ε''}(0) and B_{1+ε''}(0)); as μ ≥ Hⁿ⌞M, Θ(μ, x) ≥ 1. So Θ(μ, ·) ≥ 1 μ-a.e. in W. (ii) Θ(μ, ·) is upper semicontinuous on W: if y_j → y ∈ W and B_{τ+ε''}(y) ⊆ W, then B_τ(y_j) ⊆ B_{τ+ε''}(y) for large j and 1.2(a) gives Θ(μ, y_j) ≤ ω_n^{−1}e^{κτ}τ^{−n}μ(B_{τ+ε''}(y)); let j → ∞, then ε'' ↓ 0, then τ ↓ 0. (iii) If y ∈ spt μ ∩ W, every B̆_{1/j}(y) has positive μ-measure, hence contains x_j with Θ(μ, x_j) ≥ 1; by (ii), Θ(μ, y) ≥ 1.
1.4 Hⁿ((spt μ ∩ W) ∖ M) = 0. Let A' := (spt μ ∩ W) ∖ M, so μ(A') = 0. Given ε'' > 0 choose an open O with A' ⊆ O ⊆ W and μ(O) < ε'' (outer regularity of the Radon measure μ⌞W). For x ∈ A' the upper n-density of μ⌞O at x equals Θ(μ, x) ≥ 1, so the comparison theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.3; library simon_theorem_3_3) gives Hⁿ(A') ≤ μ(O) < ε''.
1.5 θ(x) ≤ Θ(μ, x) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ W. For an integer m ≥ 1 let M_m := {x ∈ M : θ(x) = m}. By the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 and Remark 3.7(2) for the locally finite measure Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ W); library simon_theorem_3_6), the upper density of Hⁿ⌞(M ∖ M_m) vanishes at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_m ∩ W; with 1.3(i), Hⁿ(M_m ∩ B_τ(x))/(ω_nτⁿ) → 1 there, and μ ≥ m·Hⁿ⌞M_m gives Θ(μ, x) ≥ m = θ(x).
1.6 Tangent planes on a Lipschitz graph (Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(2) and the proof of 1.6). Let S be an n-plane, a ∈ E, f : S → S^⊥ Lipschitz, Φ_f(v) := a + v + f(v), F := Φ_f(S). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ F ∩ W, writing x = Φ_f(v): f is differentiable at v and T_xM = graph Df(v) := {w + Df(v)w : w ∈ S}.
 Proof. (i) By Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt) and Lebesgue's differentiation theorem, Lⁿ-a.e. v ∈ S is a differentiability point of f and a Lebesgue point of Df; the exceptional set N satisfies Hⁿ(Φ_f(N)) = 0 because Φ_f is Lipschitz. (ii) For v ∉ N, F has approximate tangent plane graph Df(v) at x = Φ_f(v): for ψ₀ ∈ C_c(E) with spt ψ₀ ⊆ B_{R'}(0), the area formula gives ∫_{η_{x,λ}(F)} ψ₀ dHⁿ = ∫_S ψ₀(w + f_λ(w)) J_f(v + λw) dw, where f_λ(w) := (f(v + λw) − f(v))/λ and J_f is the area Jacobian of Φ_f; the integrand vanishes for |w| > R' and is uniformly bounded; f_λ → Df(v) locally uniformly and J_f(v + λ·) → J_f(v) in L¹_loc (Lebesgue point of Df; the Jacobian is a locally Lipschitz function of Df), so the integral tends to ∫_S ψ₀(w + Df(v)w) J_f(v) dw = ∫_{graph Df(v)} ψ₀ dHⁿ. (iii) By the Upper Density Theorem, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ F ∩ W the upper densities of Hⁿ⌞(F ∖ M) and of Hⁿ⌞(M ∖ F) at x vanish (both sets have locally finite Hⁿ-measure in W). (iv) At such x with v ∉ N, |∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} ψ₀ dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,λ}(F)} ψ₀ dHⁿ| ≤ sup|ψ₀|·λ^{−n}Hⁿ(((M ∖ F) ∪ (F ∖ M)) ∩ B_{λR'}(x)) → 0, so M has approximate tangent plane graph Df(v) at x, and by uniqueness (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) T_xM = graph Df(v).

Part 2. Standing assumption and density bounds (Simon 2.3–2.4).
(SA) δ ∈ (0, 1/8], ρ > 0, 0 ∈ spt μ, B_ρ(0) ⊆ W, μ(B_ρ(0)) ≤ (1 + δ)ω_nρⁿ and κρ ≤ δ. Put r₁ := δρ. As B_ρ(0) is compact and W open, fix ρ⁺ ∈ (ρ, 2ρ) with B_{ρ⁺}(0) ⊆ W. For y ∈ B_{4r₁}(0) we have B_{ρ⁺−4r₁}(y) ⊆ W and ρ⁺ − 4r₁ > (1 − 4δ)ρ ≥ ρ/2 ≥ 4r₁; so 1.1–1.2 apply at y for all radii ≤ (1 − 4δ)ρ.
2.1 For every y ∈ B_{4r₁}(0) and 0 < t ≤ (1 − 4δ)ρ: μ(B_t(y)) ≤ (1 + c(δ))ω_ntⁿ with c(δ) := e^{δ}(1 − 4δ)^{−n}(1 + δ) − 1 ≤ C₁δ. Indeed by 1.2(a) with t' := (1 − 4δ)ρ and B_{t'}(y) ⊆ B_ρ(0): t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) ≤ e^{κt'}t'^{−n}μ(B_ρ(0)) ≤ e^{δ}(1 − 4δ)^{−n}(1 + δ)ω_n.
2.2 For every y ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{4r₁}(0) and 0 < t ≤ (1 − 4δ)ρ: μ(B_t(y)) ≥ e^{−δ}ω_ntⁿ, by 1.2(a) and 1.3: e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) ≥ ω_nΘ(μ, y) ≥ ω_n. Fix δ₁ = δ₁(n) ∈ (0, 1/8] with C₁δ₁ ≤ 1/2; for δ ≤ δ₁ we get ½ω_ntⁿ ≤ μ(B_t(y)) ≤ 2ω_ntⁿ (Simon 2.4). Step 6 (transfer to ℝⁿ; Simon (14)–(16)). Let J_f(v) := (det(I + Df(v)ᵀDf(v)))^{1/2} ∈ [1, 2^{n/2}], so |J_f − 1| ≤ C|Df|², and θ_F(v) := θ(Φ_f(v)) if Φ_f(v) ∈ M, θ_F(v) := 0 otherwise. By the area formula for the injective Lipschitz map Φ_f (Simon Ch. 2, 3.5) and Step 3, for every Borel g on ℝⁿ supported in B̆ⁿ_{r/2}(0) and nonnegative or integrable: ∫_{M₁∩B_r(ξ)} g(x') dμ = ∫_{Bⁿ_{r/2}(0)} g(v)θ_F(v)J_f(v) dv. Let Z₀ := {v ∈ B̆ⁿ_{r/2}(0) : Φ_f(v) ∉ M} and Z₂ := {v ∈ B̆ⁿ_{r/2}(0) : θ_F(v) ≥ 2}. By 1.4, (4') and J_f ≥ 1: Lⁿ(Z₀) ≤ Hⁿ((F ∖ spt μ) ∩ B_r(ξ)) + Hⁿ((spt μ ∩ W) ∖ M) ≤ C₇σⁿE₀ ≤ CrⁿE₀; by 2.4, Lⁿ(Z₂) = 0. Off Z₀ ∪ Z₂ we have θ_F = 1. Hence from (12'), (13'):
 (16') r^{−n}∫_{Bⁿ_{r/2}(0)} |∇fʲ|² dv ≤ CE₀,
 (15') |r^{−n}∫_{Bⁿ_{r/2}(0)} ∇fʲ·∇ζ₀ dv| ≤ C sup|∇ζ₀|(δ^{1/2}E₀^{1/2} + E₀) ≤ C₁₂δ^αE₀^{1/2} sup|∇ζ₀|,
 using ∫_{Z₀}|∇fʲ||∇ζ₀| ≤ sup|∇ζ₀|Lⁿ(Z₀), |θ_FJ_f − 1| ≤ C|Df|² off Z₀ ∪ Z₂ together with (16'), and E₀ ≤ (C₃δ^{2α})^{1/2}E₀^{1/2}, δ^{1/2} ≤ δ^α. Correction: Simon's (15) has the factor δ^{1/2}E₀^{1/2}; since only E₀ ≤ Cδ^{1/(n+1)} is available, the factor is δ^{1/(2n+2)}E₀^{1/2}, which suffices.
Step 7 (harmonic approximation; Simon (17)). By (16') choose C₁₃ with R₀^{−n}∫_{Bⁿ_{R₀}(0)} |∇fʲ|² ≤ C₁₃E₀. Then w := (C₁₃E₀)^{−1/2}fʲ satisfies the hypotheses of 6.1 on B̆ⁿ_{R₀}(0) provided C₁₄δ^α ≤ δ_h(n, ε'), where C₁₄ := 2ⁿC₁₂C₁₃^{−1/2}. So there are harmonic functions uʲ on B̆ⁿ_{R₀}(0), j = 1, …, k, and u := (u¹, …, uᵏ) satisfies
 (17') R₀^{−n}∫_{Bⁿ_{R₀}(0)} |Du|² ≤ CE₀ and R₀^{−n−2}∫_{Bⁿ_{R₀}(0)} |f − u|² ≤ Cε'E₀.
Step 8 (affine approximation of u; Simon (18)–(19)). Let λ(v) := u(0) + Du(0)v. By 6.2, (17') and |f| ≤ C₇δ^ασ = 8C₇δ^αR₀: |Du(0)| ≤ CE₀^{1/2}, and (18') |u(0)| ≤ CR₀^{−n/2}(‖u − f‖_{L²} + ‖f‖_{L²}) ≤ C₁₅R₀δ^α; and for θ' ∈ (0, ¼], sup over Bⁿ_{θ'R₀}(0) of |u − λ| ≤ Cθ'²R₀E₀^{1/2}. Hence
 (19') (θ'R₀)^{−n−2}∫_{Bⁿ_{θ'R₀}(0)} |f − λ|² dv ≤ C(θ'^{−n−2}ε' + θ'²)E₀.
Step 9 (the new plane; Simon (20)–(22)). Let S := {(w, Du(0)w) : w ∈ ℝⁿ}, an n-plane, and τ := ξ + (0, u(0)). Require C₁₅δ^α ≤ θ'/4; then |τ − ξ| ≤ θ'R₀/4 and B_{θ'R₀}(τ) ⊆ B_{σ/2}(ξ). For x = Φ_f(v) with |v| ≤ θ'R₀, dist(x − τ, S) ≤ |f(v) − λ(v)|, and F ∩ B_{θ'R₀}(τ) ⊆ Φ_f(Bⁿ_{θ'R₀}(0)). Split ∫_{B_{θ'R₀}(τ)} dist(x − τ, S)² dμ into the parts on F and off F. On F, μ⌞F ≤ Hⁿ⌞F (θ = 1 μ-a.e. there by 2.4) and the area formula with J_f ≤ 2^{n/2} bound it by 2^{n/2}∫_{Bⁿ_{θ'R₀}(0)} |f − λ|². Off F, each x ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{θ'R₀}(τ) has dist(x − τ, S) ≤ |x''| + |u(0)| + |Du(0)||x'| ≤ Cδ^ασ by (2') and (18'), and μ(B_{θ'R₀}(τ) ∖ F) ≤ C₇σⁿE₀ by (4'). With σ = 8R₀ this gives
 (θ'R₀)^{−n−2}∫_{B_{θ'R₀}(τ)} dist(x − τ, S)² dμ ≤ C(θ'^{−n−2}ε' + θ'^{−n−2}δ^{2α} + θ'²)E₀.
 Correction: Simon's middle term Cδ^{1/(n+1)}E₀ omits the factor θ'^{−n−2}; this is harmless because θ' is fixed before δ. Now 3.1 at (τ, θ'R₀) (B_{θ'R₀}(τ) ⊆ W, μ(B_{θ'R₀}(τ)) ≤ 2ω_n(θ'R₀)ⁿ by 2.1, κ²(θ'R₀)² ≤ κ²σ² ≤ δE₀) gives
 (20') E(τ, θ'R₀/2, S) ≤ C(θ'^{−n−2}(ε' + δ^{2α}) + θ'² + δ)E₀,
 and since B_{θ'R₀/4}(ξ) ⊆ B_{θ'R₀/2}(τ) (21'),
 (22') E(ξ, θ'R₀/4, S) ≤ 2ⁿE(τ, θ'R₀/2, S) ≤ C₁₆(θ'^{−n−2}(ε' + δ^{2α}) + θ'² + δ)E₀.
Step 10 (choice of constants; Simon (23)). Put θ₀ := θ'R₀/(4σ) = θ'/32. Choose θ' ∈ (0, ¼] with C₁₆θ'² ≤ θ'/128, then ε' > 0 with C₁₆θ'^{−n−2}ε' ≤ θ'/128, then δ₂ ∈ (0, δ₁] so small that for δ ≤ δ₂: δ^α ≤ β (Step 2), C₁₁δ^α ≤ 1/16 and C₇δ^α ≤ 1/16 (Step 3), C₁₄δ^α ≤ δ_h(n, ε') (Step 7), C₁₅δ^α ≤ θ'/4 (Step 9), C₁₆θ'^{−n−2}δ^{2α} ≤ θ'/128 and C₁₆δ ≤ θ'/128. Then E(ξ, θ₀σ, S) ≤ (θ'/32)E₀ = θ₀E₀ and δ^{−1}κ²(θ₀σ)² = θ₀²δ^{−1}κ²σ² ≤ θ₀E₀, so E_*(ξ, θ₀σ, S) ≤ θ₀E_*(ξ, σ, T).

Part 8. Iteration and the graph (proof of Simon 5.2).
Assume (SA) with δ ≤ δ₂ and the smallness conditions of 8.4. Put σ₀ := r₁ = δρ.
8.1 Base plane. Part 4 at (0, 2σ₀) gives T₀ with E(0, σ₀, T₀) ≤ C₃δ^{2α} and dist(x, T₀) ≤ 2C₃δ^ασ₀ for x ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{2σ₀}(0). For ξ ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{σ₀/2}(0), B_{σ₀/2}(ξ) ⊆ B_{σ₀}(0), so E_*(ξ, σ₀/2, T₀) ≤ max{2ⁿC₃δ^{2α}, δ³} ≤ E₀ := 2ⁿC₃δ^{2α} (C₃ ≥ 1).
8.2 Iteration. Fix ξ ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{σ₀/2}(0) and put σ_j := θ₀^jσ₀/2 ∈ (0, r₁]. Applying 7A inductively at (ξ, σ_j, S_j) gives n-planes S₀ := T₀, S₁, S₂, … with E_*(ξ, σ_{j+1}, S_{j+1}) ≤ θ₀E_*(ξ, σ_j, S_j), so E_*(ξ, σ_j, S_j) ≤ θ₀^jE₀, and by 7B |p_{S_{j+1}} − p_{S_j}| ≤ (C₁₀θ₀^{−n}θ₀^jE₀)^{1/2}. Summing the geometric series, p_{S_j} converges to an orthogonal projection of rank n (the set of such projections is closed); its range is called S(ξ). Then |p_{S(ξ)} − p_{S_j}| ≤ Cθ₀^{j/2}E₀^{1/2} and |p_{S(ξ)} − p_{T₀}| ≤ CE₀^{1/2}. Correction: Simon's (2) writes η^jσ₀ for η^jσ₀/2.
8.3 Decay at all scales (Simon (7)–(8)). For 0 < s ≤ σ₀/2 choose j with σ_{j+1} < s ≤ σ_j. Then E(ξ, s, S(ξ)) ≤ 2(σ_j/s)ⁿE(ξ, σ_j, S_j) + 2s^{−n}μ(B_s(ξ))|p_{S_j} − p_{S(ξ)}|² ≤ Cθ₀^jE₀ ≤ C(s/σ₀)E₀ (as θ₀^j = 2σ_j/σ₀ < 2s/(θ₀σ₀)). Thus for ξ ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{σ₀/2}(0) and 0 < s ≤ σ₀/2:
 (7'') E(ξ, s, S(ξ)) ≤ C₁₇(s/σ₀)E₀, and (8'') E(ξ, s, T₀) ≤ 2E(ξ, s, S(ξ)) + 4ω_n|p_{S(ξ)} − p_{T₀}|² ≤ C₁₈E₀.
8.4 The graph (Simon (9)). Apply 5B at (0, σ₀, T₀, L := L₀, C₆ := 2C₃): (i) and (ii) hold by 8.1; the extra hypothesis holds by (8'') provided C₁₈2ⁿC₃δ^{2α} ≤ β'²L₀²; and 5A needs δ^α ≤ βL₀. Also require C₇δ^α ≤ 1/32. These are the smallness conditions of this part (they depend on L₀). We obtain a Lipschitz f : T₀ → T₀^⊥ with Lip f ≤ L₀, sup|f| ≤ C₇δ^ασ₀ ≤ σ₀/32 and
 (9'') spt μ ∩ B_{σ₀/8}(0) = F ∩ B_{σ₀/8}(0), F := graph_0 f = {v + f(v) : v ∈ T₀}.
 Since 0 ∈ spt μ, 0 = Φ_f(v) for some v, so v = 0 and f(0) = 0.
8.5 Tangent planes (Simon (10)). Let A := {v ∈ T₀ : |v| < σ₀/16}. For v ∈ A, |Φ_f(v)| < σ₀/16 + σ₀/32, so Φ_f(v) ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{σ₀/8}(0) by (9''). By (9''), 1.4 and θ ≥ 1, Hⁿ⌞(F ∩ B_{σ₀/8}(0)) ≤ μ; hence, using J_f ≥ 1, every μ-null set has Lⁿ-null Φ_f-preimage in A. So by 1.6, 1.4 and Lebesgue's differentiation theorem for the Radon measure μ (Mathlib ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub), for Lⁿ-a.e. v ∈ A the point ξ_v := Φ_f(v) satisfies: f is differentiable at v, ξ_v ∈ M, T_{ξ_v}M = graph Df(v), and ξ_v is a μ-Lebesgue point of x ↦ p_x. At such v, (7'') gives p_{S(ξ_v)} = p_{graph Df(v)}: indeed |p_{ξ_v} − p_{S(ξ_v)}|²·s^{−n}μ(B_s(ξ_v)) ≤ 2s^{−n}∫_{B_s(ξ_v)} |p_x − p_{ξ_v}|² dμ + 2E(ξ_v, s, S(ξ_v)) → 0 as s ↓ 0, while s^{−n}μ(B_s(ξ_v)) ≥ ω_n/2.
8.6 Projections of graphs. For linear A₁, A₂ : T₀ → T₀^⊥ with ‖A₁‖, ‖A₂‖ ≤ c₀: the T₀^⊥←T₀ block of p_{graph A} is A(I + AᵀA)^{−1}, so the corresponding block of p_{graph A₁} − p_{graph A₂} equals (A₁ − A₂)(I + A₁ᵀA₁)^{−1} + A₂(I + A₁ᵀA₁)^{−1}(A₂ᵀA₂ − A₁ᵀA₁)(I + A₂ᵀA₂)^{−1}, whose Hilbert–Schmidt norm is at least (1 + c₀²)^{−1}|A₁ − A₂| − 2c₀²√(n+k)|A₁ − A₂| ≥ ½|A₁ − A₂| when c₀ = c₀(n, k) is small (this fixes c₀ in 0.1). Hence |A₁ − A₂| ≤ 2|p_{graph A₁} − p_{graph A₂}|.
8.7 Campanato estimate (Simon (11)). Let v ∈ A be as in 8.5 and 0 < s ≤ σ₀/64. For v' ∈ Bⁿ_s(v): |Φ_f(v') − ξ_v| ≤ √2|v' − v| < 2s, and B_{2s}(ξ_v) ⊆ B_{σ₀/8}(0) since |ξ_v| < 3σ₀/32. For a.e. such v', p_{Φ_f(v')} = p_{graph Df(v')} (8.5). By 8.6 (Lip f ≤ L₀ ≤ c₀), the area formula (J_f ≥ 1), Hⁿ⌞(F ∩ B_{σ₀/8}(0)) ≤ μ and (7'') with 2s ≤ σ₀/2:
 ∫_{Bⁿ_s(v)} |Df(v') − Df(v)|² dv' ≤ 4∫_{F∩B_{2s}(ξ_v)} |p_x − p_{S(ξ_v)}|² dHⁿ ≤ 4∫_{B_{2s}(ξ_v)} |p_x − p_{S(ξ_v)}|² dμ ≤ 4(2s)ⁿC₁₇(2s/σ₀)E₀.
 For a.e. v₁, v₂ ∈ A with s := |v₁ − v₂| ≤ σ₀/64, averaging |Df(v₁) − Df(v₂)|² ≤ 2|Df(v') − Df(v₁)|² + 2|Df(v') − Df(v₂)|² over v' ∈ Bⁿ_{s/2}((v₁ + v₂)/2) ⊆ Bⁿ_s(v₁) ∩ Bⁿ_s(v₂) gives |Df(v₁) − Df(v₂)| ≤ C₁₉(|v₁ − v₂|/σ₀)^{1/2}E₀^{1/2}.
8.8 C¹ regularity. Hence Df coincides Lⁿ-a.e. on A with a uniformly continuous map g (the continuous extension of Df restricted to the full-measure set of good points). As f is Lipschitz, its distributional derivative is Df; so the mollifications f_t := f ∗ ϱ_t satisfy Df_t = g ∗ ϱ_t → g locally uniformly on A and f_t → f uniformly. Therefore f is C¹ on A with Df = g, and ‖Df‖ ≤ Lip f ≤ L₀ ≤ ε on A.
8.9 Conclusion of (★). With δ = δ_A and γρ := σ₀/16 = δρ/16: by (9''), spt μ ∩ B̆_{γρ}(0) = F ∩ B̆_{γρ}(0); every x = Φ_f(v) ∈ F ∩ B̆_{γρ}(0) has |v| = |P x| < γρ, i.e. v ∈ A. Hence spt μ ∩ B̆_{γρ}(0) = Φ_f(A) ∩ B̆_{γρ}(0), with f(0) = 0, f C¹ on A and ‖Df‖ ≤ ε on A.

Part 9. The Lean statement.
Let δ_A ∈ (0, 1/8] be the minimum of δ₂ and the smallness conditions of 8.4; it depends only on n, k and ε (through L₀). Put δ₀ := δ_A and γ := δ_A/16 ∈ (0, 1]. Let U, W, R, H, κ, ρ, z satisfy the hypotheses. Then (SA) holds at the centre z with δ := δ₀: z ∈ spt μ, B_ρ(z) ⊆ W, μ(B_ρ(z)) ≤ (1 + δ₀)ω_nρⁿ, κρ ≤ δ₀ (and κ ≥ 0 since ‖H x‖ ≤ κ). Parts 2–8, centred at z, give T₀ and f. Let (a₁, …, aₙ) and (b₁, …, b_k) be orthonormal bases of T₀ and T₀^⊥, ι(v) := Σᵢ vᵢaᵢ, ι'(w) := Σ_j w_jb_j (linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0), and u(v) := (⟨f(ιv), b_j⟩)_{j=1..k}, so ι'(u(v)) = f(ιv). Then z + ιv + ι'(u v) = z + Φ_f(ιv), u(0) = 0, u is C¹ on ball 0 (γρ) with ‖fderiv ℝ u v‖ = ‖Df(ιv)‖ ≤ ε there, and by 8.9, R.measure.support ∩ ball z (γρ) = ((fun v => z + ι v + ι' (u v)) '' ball 0 (γρ)) ∩ ball z (γρ).
proof_key_steps: Monotonicity inequalities (M1)/(M2) from the first variation with |H| ≤ κ (Simon Ch. 4, 3.17); hence Θ(μ, ·) exists, is upper semicontinuous and ≥ 1 on spt μ, Hⁿ(spt μ ∖ M) = 0 and θ ≤ Θ(μ, ·).
Density bounds ½ ≤ μ(B_t(y))/(ω_n tⁿ) ≤ 1 + Cδ and the radial tilt bound ∫|x−y|^{−n−2}|p_x^⊥(x−y)|² dμ ≤ Cδ at support points near z (Simon 2.4, enlarged range); θ = 1 a.e. near z.
Tilt bounded by height (Simon 2.1) and affine approximation (Simon 2.5) by a packing, Chebyshev and choice of a good tangent plane.
Lipschitz approximation and graph criterion (Simon 2.6–2.7) via the 5-times covering lemma, Lipschitz extension, and the monotonicity bound at points off the support (corrected radii).
Harmonic approximation (Simon 3.1–3.4) and tilt-excess decay E_*(ξ, θ₀σ, S) ≤ θ₀E_*(ξ, σ, T) with E_* = max{E, δ^{−1}κ²r²} (Simon 4.5–4.6, p = 2n).
Iteration of the decay at every point of spt μ near z gives E(ξ, s, S(ξ)) ≤ C(s/σ₀)E₀; the graph criterion makes spt μ ∩ B_{σ₀/8} the graph of f with Lip f ≤ L₀ ≤ ε.
Campanato estimate for Df gives f ∈ C^{1,1/2}; choosing orthonormal bases of T₀, T₀^⊥ yields ι, ι', u with u(0) = 0 and the graph identity on B_{γρ}(z), γ = δ₀/16.

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity cycle supported on a C¹ graph is regular at the graph's base point
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1, k ≥ 0, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} open, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) represented by an integer multiplicity triple R = (M, θ, ξ) in U (T = τ(M, θ, ξ), R.Represents T), with ∂T = 0 in U. Let ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{n+k} be linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w; z ∈ ℝ^{n+k}; s, h > 0; and u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k of class C¹ on the open ball B_s(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ with u(0) = 0. Put C := {z + ιv + ι'w : |v| < s, |w| < h} and Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'u(v). If C ⊆ U, spt μ_R ∩ C = Φ(B_s(0)) (μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M = R.measure) and z ∈ spt T, then z ∈ reg T in the sense of the contract's regularSet: z ∈ spt T and there are ρ'' > 0 with B_{ρ''}(z) ⊆ U, m ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, and an embedded C¹ n-submanifold Σ ∋ z with a continuous orientation ξ_Σ and Hⁿ(Σ ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ B_{ρ''}(z), such that T(ω) = m∫_Σ⟨ω, ξ_Σ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_{ρ''}(z).
